title: [UI Tests] Treat warnings as errors in module UI test projects

proposed_comments.title: Preserve the activation key when parsing Settings shortcuts

confidence.rationale: Actual Settings HelpText producer and native PgDn/PgUp names traced at pinned upstream. Four upstream reproduction contracts and four candidate remedy contracts executed against both complete compiled parsers; only generated parent-navigation constant was adapted. No UI/runtime claim. Existing behavior predates this PR and is explicitly nonblocking.

proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve the activation key when parsing Settings shortcuts
**Severity:** `medium`

**Scope:** Non-blocking follow-up: the separator hoist preserves this existing parser limitation; enabling warnings-as-errors did not introduce it.

**Affected code:** `.github/skills/ui-tests-migration/templates/ModuleEndToEndTests.cs` (`ParseShortcutText`); the same parser also appears in `.github/skills/ui-tests-migration/templates/TestHelper.cs` and the pattern in `.github/skills/ui-tests-migration/references/patterns-and-pitfalls.md`.

**Problem:** The current `ShortcutSeparators` split treats spaces inside a key name as separators, and both parsers silently skip tokens they do not recognize. Settings puts `HotkeySettings.ToString()` in `EditButton.HelpText`; that formatter uses the keyboard-layout names `PgDn`/`PgUp` for VK_NEXT/VK_PRIOR. Thus `Win + PgDn` is reduced to `[LWin]`, which passes the `keys.Length > 0` guard before the test sends the incomplete chord.

**Why it matters:** The generated UI test may omit the configured activation key, so it cannot reliably verify that the module opens with its actual shortcut.

**Suggested change:** In both independent parser implementations, split on `+` and trim the chord boundaries without splitting spaces within a key name; map normalized `PgDn`/`PgUp` to `Key.PageDown`/`Key.PageUp` (and accept whitespace-normalized enum names); throw `FormatException` for an unsupported token rather than silently dropping it. Keep the parser recipe in `patterns-and-pitfalls.md` aligned, without making the standalone template depend on the optional helper file.

**Verification:** Cover `Win + PgDn`, `Alt + PgUp`, and `Win + Page Down` in both parser implementations, and verify `Win + Unknown` throws instead of yielding a modifier-only chord.

actions.label: Post nonblocking parser follow-up
actions.note: Existing parser limitation, not introduced by this PR; not a merge condition or an approval.
